text:
Collin Graf scored 21 goals for San Jose last season as an undrafted free agent out of Quinnipiac. This season he has two in 22 games and four points total, and San Jose Hockey Now reported he's not happy with his start and trying to stay positive. One point in his last ten.

We'd tell him to keep doing what he's doing. He's had 4.7 expected goals (the quality of his chances) and turned only two into goals; his chance rate, 0.82 expected goals per 60, is about where it was in his 21-goal season. The Sharks are six points better in shot share with him on than off. His shooting will come back toward his norm, and our range has him somewhere between 9 and 19 goals by April.

His game is built on pace. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 52% of his shots coming off the rush last season, and he's in the 79th percentile for top speed. Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.2 wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength offense. He played 21 minutes in Saturday's 6-5 win in Utah, his most in weeks. If the minutes stay there, so will the looks.
